'''Richard Lawrence Bishop''' (August 12, 1931 – December 18, 2019) was an American [[mathematician]] who specialized in [[differential geometry]] and taught at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]].

Bishop went to [[Case Institute of Technology]] as an undergraduate, earning a B.S. in 1954. Next he earned his Ph.D. from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1959, and immediately joined the UIUC faculty,<ref>[http://www.math.illinois.edu/~bishop/ Information from Bishop's web page at UIUC], retrieved 2014-06-16.</ref> where he stayed until his retirement in 1997.<ref name="obit"/> His thesis, ''On Imbeddings and Holonomy'', was supervised by [[Isadore Singer]].<ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|name=Richard Lawrence Bishop|id=9690}}</ref> At UIUC, his doctoral students included future UIUC colleague [[Stephanie B. Alexander]].<ref name="mg"/> He is the author of ''Geometry of Manifolds'' (with Richard J. Crittenden, AMS Chelsea Publishing, 1964,<ref>Review of ''Geometry of Manifolds'' by W. Klingenberg, {{MR|0169148}}</ref> translated into Russian 1967<ref>{{MR|0213981}}</ref> and reprinted 2001<ref>1852066</ref>) and ''Tensor Analysis on Manifolds'' (with Samuel I. Goldberg, Macmillan, 1968,<ref>Review of ''Tensor Analysis on Manifolds'' by T. J. Willmore, {{MR|0224010}}</ref> reprinted by Dover Books on Mathematics, 1980<ref>{{MR|0615912}}</ref>).

In 2013, Bishop became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25  }}, retrieved 2014-06-16.</ref>

The [[Bishop–Gromov inequality]] in [[Riemannian geometry]], one form of which appeared in his book with Crittenden, is named after him and [[Mikhail Leonidovich Gromov|Mikhail Gromov]], who gave an improved formulation of Bishop's result. He introduced the "Bishop frame" of curves in Euclidean space, an alternative to the better-known [[Frenet–Serret formulas|Frenet frame]]. With [[Barrett O'Neill]] he made foundational contributions to the study of convex functions and convex sets in Riemannian geometry and their applications in the study of negative [[sectional curvature]], including to the geometry of [[warped geometry|warped products]].

==Notable publications==
* R.L. Bishop and B. O'Neill. ''Manifolds of negative curvature.'' Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 145 (1969), 1–49. {{doi|10.2307/1995057}} {{closed access}}; {{doi|10.1090/S0002-9947-1969-0251664-4}} {{free access}}
* Richard L. Bishop. [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/210222830_There_is_More_than_One_Way_to_Frame_a_Curve ''There is more than one way to frame a curve.''] Amer. Math. Monthly 82 (1975), 246–251. {{doi|10.2307/2319846}} {{closed access}}
* Richard L. Bishop and Richard J. Crittenden. ''Geometry of manifolds.'' Reprint of the 1964 original. AMS Chelsea Publishing, Providence, RI, 2001. xii+273 pp. {{ISBN|0-8218-2923-8}}; {{doi|10.1090/chel/344}} {{closed access}}
